slides: Your body isn't a machine you tune once and forget.
Every step you take adds a micro‑load to muscles and joints.
If the load stays the same, adaptation stalls and fatigue builds.
Add a fraction—5% more weight, a few extra reps, a longer stride.
Small, consistent increments keep the engine humming for life.
Values are the compass; habits are the foot‑steps.
Pick one value you can't compromise—say, curiosity.
Attach a 2‑minute micro‑task to each trigger that feeds that value.
When the trigger fires, the habit executes without decision fatigue.
Your day becomes a series of intentional moves toward what matters.
Most athletes train muscles but ignore the breath.
Oxygen delivery is the bottleneck for cellular power.
Box‑breathing before a set primes the nervous system for efficiency.
A 4‑4‑6 pattern cuts heart‑rate spikes and steadies form.
Control the inhale, and you control the output of every rep.
Stagnation often follows a silent mental drift.
A 30‑second reset pulls you out of autopilot.
Close your eyes, note three sensations, and state one intention.
The ritual rewires the prefrontal loop, sharpening focus.
Use it daily and watch inertia turn into forward pull.
